tested_scope: One bounded 24-cell finite model: four authority-freshness mechanisms crossed with force-rewind, delete/recreate, snapshot restore, stale claimant, response-loss retry, and rate-limit interruption. Same-domain rollback means the authority record and all repository-local remembered freshness state may rewind together. Sibling-witness safety is evaluated only when that sibling authority remains intact; it is separately rejected by the no-external-hosted-coordination acceptance gate.

public_sources.observation: GitHub's Update a reference endpoint accepts force=true for non-fast-forward ref movement; leaving force false requires fast-forward. The same API family exposes reference deletion. Therefore ordinary Git ancestry is not by itself an unrewindable freshness witness when force/deletion authority exists.

Protected branches block force pushes and deletions by default, but policy configuration and bypass semantics are separate from commit ancestry. Public-repository Free availability is documented; private repositories require paid plans for this feature, so plan-independent acceptance cannot be assumed from branch protection alone.

same_repository_monotonic_record.assumption: generation, transition_id, and current-blob CAS live only in the same rollback domain

sibling_repository_monotonic_witness.assumption: a distinct repository-level witness remains current and is outside the target authority rollback/delete/restore event
sibling_repository_monotonic_witness.rejection: The sibling becomes a separate hosted coordination authority. Safety is conditional on its independent survival, so this does not meet the current no-external-hosted-coordination acceptance target even when incremental monetary cost is zero.

same_repository_commit_ancestor_witness.assumption: claimant checks that current ref descends from a remembered prior commit, but the remembered prior commit identity is itself reconstructed only from repository-local state
same_repository_commit_ancestor_witness.narrowing: Ancestor checking becomes safe against rewind only if the prior tip/incarnation is anchored outside the rollback domain or force/delete/restore is authoritatively impossible. The first adds an external witness; the second is a new policy-enforcement leaf rather than a property of commit history itself.

fail_closed_without_nonrollback_freshnes.assumption: never authorize an external effect unless a freshness proof outside the possible rollback domain is available
fail_closed_without_nonrollback_freshnes.rejection: Safety by universal refusal does not reproduce the useful coordination outcome.

observations: Git references can be force-updated when explicitly requested, and refs can be deleted through the documented API.
Protected branches default to blocking force pushes and deletions, but that is a separate repository policy control with plan/bypass conditions.
inferences: A monotonic value and CAS stored entirely inside one rollback domain cannot distinguish a true old world from a later world that was completely rewound to the same bytes.
Commit ancestry is not a durable anti-rollback witness if both the ref and the remembered prior tip can rewind together.
An independent witness removes the indistinguishability in the tested rollback scope but violates the current acceptance target when it becomes a separate hosted coordination authority.
Fail-closed unknown preserves safety but not useful-outcome parity.

phase1_leaf_result.new_narrowing: Repository-local monotonic generation plus CAS remains sufficient for ordinary stale-claim/retry/rate-limit interruption, but not for complete authority-domain rewind/delete-recreate/restore. Among the four tested mechanisms, the only progress-preserving rollback-safe witness is an independent authority, which fails the no-external-hosted-coordination gate; universal fail-closed is safe but non-useful.
phase1_leaf_result.minimal_unresolved_child: Can the same repository make authority rewind/delete/recreate authoritatively impossible, with policy that is itself non-bypassable in the tested actor model and works with zero finite monthly/trial/paid quota and zero incremental cost?

scope_guard: No O/O-derived state, other-worker state/config/receipt, downstream state, legacy research, shared ledger, scheduler state, protected-primary state, or unrelated repository semantics were used. Positive/negative claims are limited to the 24 modeled cells and cited GitHub reference/protection behavior.
continuation: Part121: execute one bounded policy-enforcement model for a same-repository non-rewind authority boundary. Compare unprotected ref, protected branch default, protected branch with administrator/bypass disabled where available, and repository delete/recreate exposure under force-push, ref deletion, settings change/bypass, repository delete/recreate, stale claimant, response-loss retry, and rate-limit interruption. Treat any plan/visibility requirement, bypassable administrator path, richer-mode/manual step, finite monthly/trial/paid quota, or incremental cost as an unresolved child; persist exactly one checkpoint and no second leaf.
